summary.text: Gil Cisneros is the Democratic incumbent for California's 31st Congressional District. A Navy veteran and former Frito-Lay logistics manager, he later became a philanthropist, served one term in the U.S. House from 2019 to 2021, and was Under Secretary of Defense for Personnel and Readiness from 2021. He returned to the House after the November 2024 election and serves on the Armed Services and Small Business committees.

paragraphs.text: Cisneros was born in Los Angeles in 1971, and his official biography says he grew up in Southern California and enlisted in the U.S. Navy in 1989 after graduating from high school.

He received a Naval ROTC scholarship through the Broadened Opportunity for Officer Selection and Training Program and was commissioned an officer in 1994; Ballotpedia lists his service as a Navy supply officer from 1994 to 2004.

He earned a bachelor's degree in political science from George Washington University in 1994, an MBA from Regis University in 2002, and a master's degree in urban education policy from Brown University in 2015.

Cisneros worked as a logistics manager for Frito-Lay, and after winning the lottery in 2010 he and his wife, Jacki, established the Gilbert & Jacki Cisneros Foundation, which funds scholarships and college access programs.
In 2015 he founded the Cisneros Hispanic Leadership Institute at George Washington University, which provides scholarships for Latino students, according to his official biography.
Cisneros was elected to the U.S. House from California's 39th District in 2018 and served on the Armed Services and Veterans' Affairs committees, until he lost re-election in 2020 to Young Kim.
President Biden appointed him Under Secretary of Defense for Personnel and Readiness in April 2021, and he was sworn in on August 24, 2021, after Senate confirmation.
In April 2022 the Secretary of Defense named him the Pentagon's first Chief Diversity and Inclusion Officer.
Cisneros was elected in November 2024 to represent California's 31st District and took office in 2025.

His committee assignments are Armed Services (Intelligence and Special Operations and Military Personnel subcommittees) and Small Business, where he is ranking member of the Contracting and Infrastructure Subcommittee.

According to his official pages, he co-founded the Military Transition Assistance Pathway (MTAP) Caucus and co-chairs the Military Mental Health Caucus, and the U.S. Navy Memorial and the Navy Supply Corps Foundation have recognized his service.
